prompt: In wallet-helper/, the tools in app/tools/wallet.py call our wallet service over JSON-RPC, but its API is not declared yet, so lint refuses them. Its URL is in WALLET_RPC_URL and it takes a bearer token from WALLET_RPC_TOKEN. Declare it so the agent can send exactly the methods those tools use and nothing else. Don't change the tools.

checks.expr: get(data, 'apis.wallet_rpc.protocol') == 'jsonrpc' and get(data, 'apis.wallet_rpc.base_url_env') == 'WALLET_RPC_URL' and get(data, 'apis.wallet_rpc.auth') == 'bearer' and get(data, 'apis.wallet_rpc.token_env') == 'WALLET_RPC_TOKEN' and get(data, 'apis.wallet_rpc.allowed_methods') == ['POST']
checks.why: a JSON-RPC API is declared as one (`api add NAME --protocol jsonrpc`), so each POST is judged by the method in its body; the tools' API_CALLS name the API wallet_rpc

checks.expr: (lambda ops: bool(ops) and all(isinstance(o, dict) and o.get('rpc_method') in ('wallet.balance', 'wallet.history') and o.get('path') == '/rpc' and [str(m).upper() for m in (o.get('methods') or [])] == ['POST'] for o in ops) and {o.get('rpc_method') for o in ops} == {'wallet.balance', 'wallet.history'})(get(data, 'apis.wallet_rpc.allowed_operations') or [])
checks.why: on a JSON-RPC API every call is a POST to one endpoint: an entry without rpc_method allows every method there (`api allow NAME --rpc-method M --method POST --path /rpc`)
`api add` puts a bearer token_env into secrets.keys

reference: `graph-agents-cli api add wallet_rpc --protocol jsonrpc --base-url-env WALLET_RPC_URL --auth bearer --token-env WALLET_RPC_TOKEN --access custom --methods POST` (--dry-run first), then `graph-agents-cli api allow wallet_rpc --rpc-method wallet.balance --method POST --path /rpc` and the same for wallet.history, the two methods app/tools/wallet.py declares in API_CALLS. An allow entry by path alone would let every JSON-RPC method through; declaring the API as plain HTTP makes lint refuse the tools' rpc_method calls. Tools unchanged; `lint` passes.
